summary: Local decision engine for agents that answers typed questions about text, images or audio with calibrated probabilities and can abstain.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: laya makes typed decisions (choices, scores and yes/no answers) about text, images, audio and video in one forward pass on your own machine. Instead of generating text, it returns calibrated probabilities, a prediction set and an honest abstain flag when it shouldn't decide.
sixtySeconds.problem: Using a full LLM to route a ticket or score urgency is slow, costly and inconsistent. laya gives fast, deterministic, typed answers with confidence.
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for local, constant-cost decisions with probabilities and abstention, 73k tokens of context, and optional server, MCP and LangChain extras.

overview: Create laya.Agent() and call predict with your input and a dictionary of questions. Each question has a type (choice, score or noul for yes/no), instructions and criteria; answers include the choice, probabilities and a prediction set.
Since 0.5.0 the default engine is a frozen 0.8B reader with a small 'physics' layer; you can switch readers (for example a 4B model) with one string, or use laya's own encoders.
laya is Apache 2.0 and free for any use. Continuous learning (laya.Learner and related) needs the separate vegaml-learn package, which is noncommercial only.

useCases.title: Urgency scoring
useCases.body: Rate how urgent a message is.

install.verificationNote: Commands come from laya's README. AIRepoHub hasn't run them yet.

firstRun.title: Route a support message
firstRun.code:
import laya

agent = laya.Agent()
out = agent.predict("We were billed twice for March. Refund it today or we cancel.",
    {"department": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Which department should handle this?",
                    "criteria": {"billing": "invoices, refunds", "technical": "bugs, outages"}}})
print(out["answers"]["department"]["choice"])

tutorial.title: Make several decisions about one message
tutorial.useCase: Get department, urgency and churn risk at once.

steps.title: Define questions
steps.code:
questions = {
    "department": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Which department should handle this?",
                   "criteria": {"billing": "invoices, payments, refunds", "technical": "bugs, outages", "other": "everything else"}},
    "urgency": {"type": "score", "instructions": "How urgent is this?",
                "criteria": ["not urgent", "soon", "blocking"]},
    "churn_risk": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Does the user threaten to cancel or leave?"},
}

steps.title: Predict
steps.code:
import laya
agent = laya.Agent()
out = agent.predict("Hi, we were billed twice for March. Please refund the duplicate today or we will cancel our plan.", questions)
print(out["answers"])

tutorial.expected: Typed answers with probabilities, for example department billing.
